newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart expands office wares to vie with Staples.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart expands office wares to vie with Staples.

text.p: The president of Wal-Mart Stores Inc said in videotaped testimony played Wednesday in a U.S. District Court hearing on the proposed merger of Staples and Office Depot that his chain is expanding its offerings of office supplies.

The videotaped deposition was presented by Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc answering a government charge that they would have the power to raise prices if their proposed $4 billion merger wins approval. The Federal Trade Commission took the superstores to court to stop the merger.
But the lawyers for the two office supply superstores argue that Wal-Mart competes with them and offered the videotaped deposition of Wal-Mart chief executive David Glass.
"We have expanded office supplies year by year for the past several years," Glass said. Asked if the office superstores were competition, Glass replied:
"Anyone who sells anything that we do is a competitor."
Lawyers for Staples and Office Depot offered testimony that Wal-Mart now carries upwards of 2,500 different kinds of office and home stationary items, with hundreds more scheduled to be added.
By contrast, office superstores carry about 6,000 to 6,500 different kinds of items.

An official of Office Depot said during a break that the same 2,500 items Wal-Mart chooses to sell are those which account for about 80 percent or more of the dollar volume for Office Depot and Staples.
The hearing before U.S. District Judge Thomas Hogan runs through Friday. Hogan has said he will decide by mid-June whether to grant a preliminary injunction against the merger.
